title: Check yourself: where access modifiers may be written

questions.stem: Which access modifiers does this page allow on a top-level class, one that is not nested in another class?

options.says: The page's answer A2: only public and default can be applied to a top-level class.

options.text: public, or protected for subclass use
options.says: A2 says protected has no meaning for a top-level class, which is a member of a package, not of a class.
A2 rules out both private and protected on a top-level class; all four apply only to nested classes.

questions.stem: According to this page, on which of these declarations can no access modifier be written?

options.text: A constructor of a public class
options.says: Key point 1 lists constructors among the things access modifiers apply to, as the singleton's private constructor shows.

options.text: A variable local to one method
options.says: Key point 1: access modifiers apply to classes, methods, fields and constructors, not to local variables.

options.text: A class nested inside another class
options.says: Key point 4: inner classes can use all four access modifiers.
